name: Hospital Queue
description: There are $$$n$$$ people (numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$) signed up for a doctor's appointment. The doctor has to choose in which order he will appoint these people. The $$$i$$$-th patient should be appointed among the first $$$p_i$$$ people. There are also $$$m$$$ restrictions of the following format: the $$$i$$$-th restriction is denoted by two integers $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$ and means that the patient with the index $$$a_i$$$ should be appointed earlier than the patient with the index $$$b_i$$$. For example, if $$$n = 4$$$, $$$p = [2, 3, 2, 4]$$$, $$$m = 1$$$, $$$a = [3]$$$ and $$$b = [1]$$$, then the only order of appointment of patients that does not violate the restrictions is $$$[3, 1, 2, 4]$$$. For $$$n =3$$$, $$$p = [3, 3, 3]$$$, $$$m = 0$$$, $$$a = []$$$ and $$$b = []$$$, any order of appointment is valid. For each patient, calculate the minimum position in the order that they can have among all possible orderings that don't violate the restrictions.
input_specification:
The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2000$$$; $$$0 \le m \le 2000$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$). Then $$$m$$$ lines follow. The $$$i$$$-th of them contains two integers $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le n$$$; $$$a_i 
e b_i$$$). All pairs of $$$(a_i, b_i)$$$ are distinct (i. e. if $$$i 
e j$$$, then either $$$a_i 
e a_j$$$, $$$b_i 
e b_j$$$, or both). Additional constraint on the input: there is at least one valid order of patients.
output_specification: Print $$$n$$$ integers, where $$$i$$$-th integer is equal to the minimum position of $$$i$$$-th patient in the order, among all valid orders. Positions in the order are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1765H — Hospital Queue [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
